recordedOn: Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.5.2, Node 22.23.1 (the flake devShell's node — the version CI runs; recorded with `nix develop --command pnpm bench`). Each figure is the median of TEN whole-benchmark runs, not five and not one: the machine was under heavy concurrent load (load average 17-42) and a five-run sample put one workload's spread at 479%, which is not a median anyone should commit. Ten runs brings the interquartile spread to 6.5-63%. See the note for what that does and does not invalidate.
note: guards are slow/fast A/B ratios measured in one process against one data set: the machine cancels, so these are the real gate (tolerance 1.30, except the shipped-vs-frozen gate at 1.15). workloads are workload/yardstick ratios and are only approximately machine-independent — indicative, not authoritative (tolerance 2.0). WHAT MOVED IN THIS RECORDING, AND WHY: two features landed. (1) AMBIENT OCCLUSION (domain/ambient-occlusion.ts, docs/design-notes.md M-10). AO is computed once per EXPOSED FACE and joins the greedy merge key, so it costs time in both meshers and costs quads in the merged one. (2) CROSS-PLATE PLANTS (domain/plant-mesh.ts, M-11), which add one byte-indexed table read to `isFaceExposed` — the ~400k calls/chunk path plan.md §3.3 measures. Against the previous recording `meshChunk/*` is 1.08-1.12x and `meshChunkNaive/*` is 1.13-1.17x, except meshChunk/checkerboard-worst at 0.92x. THE ATTRIBUTION WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, because under this much load the raw medians cannot carry it: interleaved paired runs (pre-feature and post-feature alternating on the same machine, yardstick 1.01-1.02x between the two arms) put AO at 1.26-1.36x of `meshChunk` (1.94-2.05x on checkerboard) and the plant lookup at a further 1.08-1.09x (0.98x on checkerboard, which short-circuits on AIR most often and so reaches the extra read least). The previous baseline had already absorbed AO; what this recording adds on top of it is the plant read. `simplifyMesh/*` came in at 0.90-0.97x, i.e. unmoved within the noise — nothing in either feature touches it, and its flat/layered rows are at the measurement floor (0.016-0.018 ms/chunk against a ~0.2 ms yardstick) where the ratio carries no information at all. GUARDS DID NOT MOVE and were not expected to: neither feature touches any of them, and all five land within 0.97-1.08x. ON SPREAD: across the ten recording runs the interquartile spread was 7.5-31.7% for guards and 6.5-63.0% for workloads. That is worse than any previous recording and it is the concurrent load, not the code. A workload run that lands just inside the 2.0 gate is not evidence of anything. ON NODE VERSIONS: the same benchmark on Node 24.13.0 puts the workload ratios well above these. The recorded environment is Node 22; comparing across major versions is not meaningful. Regenerate with `pnpm bench --update-baseline` and say in the commit message what moved and why.
